summary: logger-libs executes obfuscated payload reassembled from 100+ shard files at import time
details: logger_libs/helper.py reconstructs a hidden payload by concatenating base64 fragments from logger_libs/themes/theme_000..099.py and logger_libs/ansi/*.py in a scrambled order, XOR-decoding the result with hardcoded keys (b'palette-build-2024', b'ansi-const-7f3a'), base64-decoding again, and passing the resulting source to the exec builtin. The exec sink itself is disguised in logger_libs/_compat.py, which resolves exec indirectly via getattr(builtins, chr(101)+chr(120)+chr(101)+chr(99)) and exposes it as a see_namespace()/load_module() helper. The namespace handed to exec pre-binds requests, subprocess, sys, os, ctypes.wintypes and a 'url' value, so the decoded code can perform arbitrary network and OS operations on the installer's machine. This reassemble-xor-exec chain fires during class-body evaluation of LogHelper, which is the sole advertised API, so any `import logger_libs` or `from logger_libs.helper import LogHelper` triggers execution. Metadata is also inconsistent in a typosquat-shaped way: setup.py declares name 'logger_libs' but points url to https://github.com/wolf1986/logger_libss (double 's'), while README and badges reference 'log-utils' / 'logger_util'.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
